description: Single-DGX-Spark Qwen3.8-27B on Ash Hart's TensorFold 1.2.3, the native Zig engine from the creator's linux-aarch64 release archive (exact decoding; its CUDA kernels, sm_121 included, are built into the binary, so nothing compiles at start), with turboderp's EXL3 3.00 bits-per-weight pack (branch 3.00bpw, 13.8 GB) and z-lab's DFlash2 draft model, launched as upstream documents it (serve the checkpoint with --drafter naming DFlash2). Upstream's native CUDA engine reads turboderp's dense EXL3 packs (mul1 codebook) with DFlash2 drafts on one GPU. One rank. Upstream's serve defaults apply: a 32,768-token context (raise the context setting up to the model's 262,144 tokens, subject to TensorFold's startup memory check) and --parallel auto, which shares decode rounds among up to eight streams as memory allows and reports the accepted count at startup. Text only (no image option). Upstream measured 45.8 tok/s chat and 71.9 tok/s code with DFlash2 on one GB10 with the 4.00 bpw branch (TensorFold 1.2.0, #1465; another branch, upstream claims, unmeasured here). Other branches are different weights and would be a different recipe. Needs NVIDIA driver R580 or newer (CUDA 13.0). Structured output and required tool calls use the archive's libtfgrammar (xgrammar 0.2.8). The declared memory envelope is carried over from the 0.6.6 recipe and is an estimate until the hardware sweep measures this engine. Licences, for information: Qwen3.8-27B and turboderp's EXL3 pack are Apache-2.0; z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 states Apache-2.0 on its model card (a mirror of incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2); TensorFold is Apache-2.0 from 0.6.0 (MIT up to 0.5.0). Thinking is chosen per request (chat template kwargs or sampling parameters), not as a recipe option; server default: Open a think block by default (upstream default: --thinking).
title: Qwen3.8 27B EXL3 3.00bpw TensorFold single Spark
